newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HORN SAYS LOOKING TO SETTLE DAM ROW WITH SLOVAKIA.
newsitem.headline: HORN SAYS LOOKING TO SETTLE DAM ROW WITH SLOVAKIA.

text.p: Hungary's prime minister Gyula Horn on Tuesday confirmed that Hungary and Slovakia were exploring an out-of-court settlement to their dispute over Slovakia's decision to divert Danube waters in a dam project.
"The Slovak attitiude has changed," Horn told reporters on Tuesday. "There is now an attitude to the negotiation that we should try to reach an agreement -- this is a very constructive standpoint."
Meciar and Horn met on Monday after a trilateral meeting of the heads of government of Austria, Hungary and Slovakia in the west Slovak spa town of Piestany.

The countries are in dispute over Slovakia's decision to unilaterally divert a considerable part of the Danube waters for its Gabcikovo hydro-electric dam project after Hungary in 1989 quit a joint deal which planned a similar dam downstream at Nagymaros in Hungary.

Slovakia claims Hungary breached its contract while the Hungarians say diverting the water breaks international law and has caused environmental damage to the marsh region of Szigetkoz, in north-western Hungary.
They had agreed to bring their case to the International Court in the Hague, which is due to consider it early next year.
A spokeswoman for Meciar told journalists after the bilateral meeting on Monday both sides saw room for settlement of the dispute.

Horn said on Tuesday that a committee would be set up to explore an out-of-court deal and its make-up finalised by the two countries' foreign ministers at the Central European Initiative summit at Graz, in Austria, this coming weekend.
"There is no guarantee that agreement can be reached but in things which are taken to the Hague, the court looks benevolently on the fact that two parties try to reach agreement" Horn said.
